intro: Eight states from Day 1. Match each one to the region it actually sat in, about 1750 — not the region its size might suggest.

right.label: Southeastern Europe, southwest Asia, and North Africa

rationale.a: The Ottoman Empire ruled from southeastern Europe through southwest Asia into North Africa — the one empire on this list that reached across three continents.
rationale.b: The Mughal Empire ruled most of the Indian subcontinent — South Asia.
rationale.c: Qing China was the largest and richest state in the world by almost any measure you can name, sitting in East Asia.
rationale.d: Tokugawa Japan sat east of China and had deliberately shut itself off from nearly all foreign contact — same region as Qing China, East Asia, a very different relationship with the rest of the world.
rationale.e: The Russian Empire was pushing east across Asia in 1750 — a land empire spanning northern Europe and northern Asia.
rationale.f: Benin was one of the wealthy, well-organized kingdoms on the West African coast, trading gold, ivory, pepper, art, and captured people with Europeans who arrived by sea.
rationale.g: Ashanti was one of the wealthy, well-organized kingdoms on the West African coast, trading gold, ivory, pepper, art, and captured people with Europeans who arrived by sea.
